text:
Anya: Quick request — I'm about to run a scrubbed production trace emulation focused on kernel selection, batching heuristics and KV behavior. Need a short QA checklist for determinism/parity and a sampling plan so apples-to-apples with synthetic runs. Can someone sanity-check?

Devin: SG. High-level plan: 1) deterministic seed + manifest 2) stratified sampling by model/seq_len/cohort 3) replicate KV warmup policy 4) capture token-level hashes + latency buckets 5) force same kernel flags. Start small (5k) then scale. :+1:

Mason: Add: log batch boundaries and kernel picks per request. Our adaptive batcher can hide regressions if you only measure avg batch size. Also record per-batch token counts.

Devin: Example harness invocation to keep runs comparable:
```
./trace_playback \  --input scrubbed-trace.jsonl \  --sample 5000 \  --stratify "model,seq_len,cohort" \  --seed 202403 \  --anon-map anon_map.json \  --kernel-flag "kernel=auto,quant=none" \  --kv-warmup 20 \  --emit-batch-logs \  --record-token-hash sha256 \
```

Anya: For anonymization: we keep order and timestamps but map user ids -> ephemeral ids and redact free-text PII. That preserves KV warmup semantics.

Priya: Parity checks I usually run: compute token-level diffs + session-level checksum. Acceptance criteria: token-mismatch <= 0.05% OR <= 10 non-overlapping token diffs per 10k requests. Latency SLO: p50/p95 within +/-10% of baseline for same hardware. If mismatch > threshold, run bit-for-bit tokenizer+ids comparison.

Mason: Did a quick smoke swapping in fast-kernel-v2 on a tiny sample and saw a regression when KV was cold — p95 jumped. Paste from local run: 
```
run summary: sample=1000 seed=202403
kernel=fast-kernel-v2
kv_warmup=20
p50=34ms p95=82ms
cpu_gpu_util=88%/72%
token_mismatch=2 (0.2%)
```

Anya: 0.2% mismatch > threshold — could be nondeterminism or kernel bug. Any hypotheses?

Devin: Two likely sources: 1) FP to int rounding in the new attention kernel for long sequences, 2) RNG state not seeded for dropout-like ops in eval path. Quick mitigation: rerun with --force-fp32-eval and set KERNEL_RNG_SEED=202403. Also add per-layer checksum.

Priya: I'll run a stratified 10k with batch-boundary logs and two kernel variants (baseline, fast-kernel-v2) and produce a diff report: token-diff histogram, per-session mismatches, batch size distribution, kv-hit-rate over first 50 tokens. ETA ~2h. Assigning to @Priya.

Mason: Also capture kernel-selection trace: which kernel chosen per invocation + reason (latency vs memory). That helped last time to pinpoint a heuristic bug.

Anya: Great. After Priya run, we should: 1) triage any non-determinism -> reproduce with minimal example, 2) if deterministic difference, file perf/regression with kernel stack + perf profile, 3) re-run with KV prefill heuristics toggled.

Priya: Short checklist I'm running (copy):
- sample size: 10k stratified by model, seq_len buckets (<=256, 256-1024, >1024)
- seed: 202403 (all steps)
- anon: map user->ephemeral, remove PII fields, keep timestamps
- kv_warmup: 20 steps, log kv_hit_rate per token index
- batching: emit per-batch size + batch composition
- kernel flags: baseline & candidate with identical quantization/flags
- captures: token-level sha256, per-request latency ms, kernel name, batch_id
- parity checks: token-mismatch%, per-session checksum, p50/p95 compare
- artifacts: raw logs + condensed csv for diffs + perf flamegraphs

infra-bot: CI job triggered: ci/trace-emulation/2369876543 (queued). ETA ~120m.

Anya: Perfect. Thanks all — @Priya post the diff summary when done and we'll decide whether to block fast-kernel-v2 canary. :eyes:
